frontMatter.title: Phase 11 evidence: typed runtime commands, notices and private replies, managed UX (commands-notices row)

summary: Phase 11 built the typed command and notice path on feature/mega-maestro-v1.1.0-rc in the Maestro checkout (macOS, Darwin 27, Node v26.12.1, git 2.54.0): the typed runtime command contract and its binding to this tenant, enrollment, installation, process epoch, registered actor, advertised capability, applied policy revision, validity window and known run, the durable command ledger (one record per id, nonce and idempotency key enrollment-wide, accepted turned unknown by a restart) and the executor over injected ports, the desktop command service (cancel revokes the run's live leases through the dispatch authority, report answers metadata, refresh re-attaches; pause and resume not composed and refused by name; no desktop prompt port), the notice inbox seam on the host adapter and its client over a receipt ledger (list, hold the unexpired, delivered once, read, acknowledged and a private reply recorded durably before the request leaves, duplicates answered from history, the body on the person's surface and nowhere on disk), the managed-state projection and the local-release gate, the Mega-Maestro settings pane with the managed status and the notice inbox surfaces, and the desktop composition of all of it (ledgers read before the attach, notices listed again on every accepted attachment, one drain at quit). Phase 11 added 43 tests in 06/06A/06A1/06B/06C over those seams. Deterministic coverage over the real executor, the real ledgers on real files, the real command and inbox services, the real lifecycle, socket client and fake daemon, the IPC handler and preload, the hooks and both renderer surfaces is green (see commands). The journey was exercised for REAL on this host over the real desktop composition (createEnterpriseService over a fake seal and anchor: sealed identity store, enrollment lifecycle registered over a unix socket, policy status, host adapter, broker dispatch bridge with its receipts ledger, command service, inbox client, every ledger a real file in a temp data directory) against a LABELED DOUBLE of the daemon whose noticeList and inbox operations validated every request with the sibling's real @mega-maestro/contracts package and answered contract-valid notices and receipts deduplicated by idempotency key: notices listed across two pages on the accepted attachment, the expired one dropped, delivered recorded once per held notice and never again, read, acknowledged and a private reply over the socket with the reply text reaching the double and never a ledger file, a duplicate answered from history with no request, an unknown message and an untyped action refused before any request, an endpoint denial kept as a denial, a dropped daemon leaving the act unavailable and the resend after the re-attach going under the same idempotency key; cancel_run revoked the live lease of a REAL child process admitted through the real bridge against the double's broker decision, the child exited on SIGTERM and was observed gone, the receipt says revoked, the duplicate was answered from history with one revocation and a cancel of an ended run was no-effect; report_status completed with metadata alone (no path, no program, no prompt), refresh_policy re-attached over the socket and completed on the applied revision and failed naming both on a desired one the endpoint does not apply; pause and resume refused by name; an operator prompt refused on the desktop by capability, refused approval-required without a bound approval, accepted only under a bound approval against a live run with its text reaching the harness port and nowhere else; and stale or replayed control (another process epoch, an unknown run, a lapsed window, another actor, another tenant, a policy behind, a reused id under another payload, a consumed nonce, a consumed idempotency key, an untyped action, a bare string) denied by name with no record and the leases untouched. Two facts keep the commands-notices row from passing: over the REAL service every command is refused unauthenticated because the registration Maestro redeems names no actor (CP-01/CP-04), so the command effects above ran under the real lifecycle's standing with the missing actor id supplied by the harness and the command handed to receive() by the harness (no producer delivers a command to a Maestro runtime: the daemon serves no command operation and its command runtime executes against neutral sessions it binds itself, CP-02); and the real sibling daemon in its container (library 0.24.0) again answered every step denied or unavailable (unenrolled, no approval producer, no notice custody), so NO central receipt exists for any notice, reply or command. pause_run and resume_run have no desktop producer (named, not approximated by a stop). The row is therefore NOT passed; the fixture journey is recorded as positive evidence at the Maestro boundary, not as the pair.

realFixtureRun.what: The typed command and notice journey over the REAL Maestro desktop composition and transport on this host, against a LABELED DOUBLE of the endpoint daemon. Real: createEnterpriseService (the one desktop composition, Electron bound only through a SafeStorageLike over the fakeSeal and an AnchorStore over the fakeAnchor): the sealed identity store on a real file, the enrollment lifecycle (recover, completeRegistration: challenge and redeem over the socket, attach), the policy status service (refresh is a real re-attach), the host adapter, createLocalEndpointClient registered and attached over a unix socket with execution, inbox and noticeList negotiated, the broker dispatch bridge and its receipts ledger file, the command service and its ledger file, the inbox client and its receipt ledger file, the onAttached hook that lists the notices after every accepted attachment, the local authority's lease (bound to a real pid, revoked by the cancel port), a REAL child process (node -e setInterval) as the cancel target, createCommandService a second time over the same real lifecycle, host, policy, dispatch and inventory with a harness prompt port and a harness ledger file. Double: fakeEndpoint.ts (the daemon protocol transcribed from the sibling: envelopes, per-socket sessions, correlation replay, registration handshake) whose noticeList and inbox operations validated every request with the sibling's real contract package (@mega-maestro/contracts dist, read-only: noticeListRequest, inboxRequest) and answered values the same package validated (notice, noticeListResult, inboxReceipt), holding one receipt per idempotency key the way a durable inbox answers a resend, and whose execution operation answered the broker decision the bridge records. Labeled too: the actor id on the standing the harness command service reads (the real registration names none: CP-01/CP-04), the source of every command (receive() called by the harness: no delivery producer, CP-02), the prompt port (the desktop composes none), and the sink that stops the child on lease revocation (the harness plays it; the ProcessManager sink is phase 06 evidence).

the operator prompt port (a harness port that records the text; the desktop composes none)

realPairRun.reading: Answer for answer the phase 04 to 10 runs, now with the 0.24.0 library bundle: peer authentication, the daemon and the socket contract work; compatibility and attachment are denied unauthenticated, the registration challenge is unavailable (no approval producer), admission is unavailable, zero leases, management unenrolled with an empty capability list. notPerformed: Against the REAL endpoint, server, API or console: the daemon is unenrolled, provisions no notice custody and serves no command operation, so no central receipt exists for any notice, reply or command (realPairRun).
A pause or a resume of a running turn: the desktop has no main-process producer for either (DESKTOP_UNCOMPOSED_COMMANDS), so both are refused by name and no effect exists to compare.
An operator prompt reaching an agent: the desktop composes no prompt port by design (nothing writes to a composer, a queue or a model); the harness port only records the text.

The fixture journey took two attempts: the first ran 7 of 8 cases and failed the endpoint-denial case on the harness's own expectation (the client keeps the endpoint's denied/unavailable answer as a denial with its reason, it does not report it as unavailable); the expectation was corrected to the client's published outcome and the second run was 8/8. The runner rewrote steps-fixture.json and vitest-fixture.log on the rerun, so the first attempt is recorded here from its output.

The first focused run (Working/11-verify/vitest-focused-attempt1-under-load.log, steps-focused-attempt1.json: 2 failed files, 3 failed tests of 731) ran while the checks batch was building the library and the CLI: two dispatch.test.ts assertions read the receipts ledger file before its coalesced write landed (effect admitted instead of released; pid null instead of 99) and the docs-examples version test failed on the stale docs line. dispatch.test.ts alone passed 7/7 at once (Working/11-verify/dispatch-alone.log); the docs line was repaired in fbc64cf0d (MRC-11-07A); the focused and library batches were rerun serially at that HEAD and are the runs recorded in commands.
The first library run (Working/11-verify/vitest-lib-attempt1-before-docs-repair.log: 1 failed of 70, 1 skipped) failed the same docs version test; rerun green after the repair.
The phase 04 to 10 pair runs remain under their own Working/*-verify folders.
